stories.headline: Intel launches $15B stock offering, its first public share sale since 1971

key_facts.fact: Intel announced on August 10, 2026 a $15 billion underwritten public offering of common stock, with proceeds going to general corporate purposes including capital expenditures and working capital.
key_facts.excerpt: SANTA CLARA, Calif., August 10, 2026 - Intel Corporation (Nasdaq: INTC) today announced a $15 billion underwritten public offering of common stock. Intel intends to use the net proceeds from the offering for general corporate purposes, which may include, but are not limited to, capital expenditures and working capital.

key_facts.fact: Underwriters get a 30-day option to buy up to $2.25 billion in additional shares, which would take the deal to $17.25 billion; J.P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Citigroup are joint book-running managers.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel expects to grant to the underwriters of the offering a 30-day option to purchase up to an aggregate total of $2.25 billion of additional shares of common stock at the public offering price, less underwriting discounts. J.P. Morgan Securities LLC, Goldman Sachs & Co. LLC, Morgan Stanley & Co. LLC and Citigroup Global Markets Inc., are acting as joint book-running managers.

key_facts.fact: Intel framed the raise around AI demand, citing physical AI, purpose-built silicon, advanced packaging and external wafers as growth opportunities, and said the offering preserves its investment-grade rating.
key_facts.excerpt: "Progress in emerging areas including physical AI, purpose-built silicon, advanced packaging and external wafers represent significant growth opportunities for Intel," the company said in a statement.

key_facts.fact: The sale follows Intel's July guidance hike, which lifted 2026 capital spending to $20 billion from $18 billion after its fastest revenue growth in nearly 15 years.
key_facts.excerpt: In July, Intel lifted its capital spending target for the year to $20 billion from $18 billion, and the company has pledged to bring its 14A manufacturing process to high-volume output by 2028. Tesla has signed on as a customer for Intel's 14A process through its foundry division.

key_facts.fact: Intel shares fell about 3% premarket on the dilution news, after rising more than 400% over the previous 12 months.
key_facts.excerpt: Intel's stock was down 3% in premarket action on Monday morning. Shares have surged more than 400% over the past 12 months.

stories.headline: Sony and TSMC to spend $6.3B on an image-sensor joint venture in Kumamoto

key_facts.fact: Sony Group and TSMC plan to spend around 1 trillion yen ($6.32 billion) to jointly make next-generation image-sensor chips, Nikkei reported on August 10, 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: TOKYO, Aug 10 (Reuters) - Sony Group and Taiwan's TSMC plan to spend around 1 trillion yen ($6.32 billion) to jointly make next-generation microchips used in image sensors, the Nikkei business daily said on Monday.

key_facts.fact: The joint venture will be about 60% owned by Sony and 40% by TSMC, and is to start commercial production as early as 2029 in Kumamoto prefecture in southern Japan.
key_facts.excerpt: A joint venture owned about 60% by Sony and 40% by TSMC will start commercial production as early as 2029 in southern Japan's Kumamoto prefecture, the paper said.

key_facts.fact: The plan converts a non-binding memorandum the two signed in May 2026 to set up development and production lines at Sony's newly built fab in Koshi City, Kumamoto, with Sony as controlling shareholder.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the proposed partnership, Sony and TSMC intend to establish a joint venture ("JV"), with Sony being the majority and controlling shareholder, to set up development and production lines in Sony's newly constructed fab in Koshi City, Kumamoto Prefecture.

key_facts.fact: Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki called the deal the company's first step toward becoming 'fab-light', a break with its decades-long practice of designing and manufacturing sensors entirely in-house.
key_facts.excerpt: with Sony CEO Hiroki Totoki describing the deal as the company's "first step to becoming fab-light" — the first structural departure from Sony's decades-long practice of designing, developing, and manufacturing its sensors entirely in-house.

key_facts.fact: Sony is the world's largest maker of image sensors used in smartphones and cameras; the Kumamoto cluster also hosts TSMC's JASM logic fab.
key_facts.excerpt: Sony is the world's largest maker of image sensors used in smartphones and cameras, while TSMC is the world's largest contract chipmaker.

stories.headline: Microsoft plans Maia 300 AI chip reveal and seeks TSMC capacity for 300,000+ units

key_facts.fact: Microsoft plans to unveil its next-generation AI chip, the Maia 300, as soon as September 2026, according to The Information, reported on August 10.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft is preparing to unveil its Maia 300 chip. The unveiling is expected this fall, possibly as early as next month. The company is negotiating with TSMC for production capacity for over 300,000 units, with delivery scheduled for 2027. The Information reported this on Monday, citing sources with direct knowledge of the plans.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft is in talks with TSMC for capacity of more than 300,000 Maia 300 chips for 2027 delivery, with a longer-term goal of more than 1 million units.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has been talking with TSMC about securing manufacturing capacity for more than 300,000 Maia 300 chips scheduled for delivery in 2027, The Information reported. Microsoft's longer-term goal is capacity for more than 1 million units, though component availability and continuing negotiations with TSMC could limit those plans.

key_facts.fact: Microsoft hopes to win big cloud customers such as Anthropic onto its own silicon; the Maia 300 is said to deliver over 30% more tokens per dollar than current hardware.
key_facts.excerpt: The Maia 300 chip is said to deliver over 30% more tokens per dollar compared to Microsoft's current hardware, and the tech giant has been in talks with TSMC about a 2027 capacity allocation.

key_facts.fact: The predecessor Maia 200, unveiled in January 2026, is built on TSMC's 3nm process with more than 140 billion transistors, over 10 petaFLOPS at 4-bit precision in a 750-watt budget, 216GB of HBM3e and 272MB of on-chip SRAM, and was designed for inference.
key_facts.excerpt: The Maia 200 is manufactured using TSMC's 3nm process and contains more than 140 billion transistors. The chip delivers over 10 petaFLOPS in 4-bit precision within a power budget of 750 watts, and features 216GB of HBM3e memory and 272MB of on-chip SRAM. Microsoft explicitly designed the accelerator for inference, not training.

key_facts.fact: Azure Maia general manager Andrew Wall said Maia 300 is expected sometime in 2027 and that Maia 200 should stay in use for another four to five years.
key_facts.excerpt: Andrew Wall, General Manager of Azure Maia, told Techzine that Maia 300 is expected sometime in 2027. However, he expects the Maia 200 to remain in use for another four to five years.

stories.headline: Anthropic, Macquarie and GIC form Theseus to build and lease AI data centers

key_facts.fact: Anthropic, Macquarie Asset Management and Singapore's GIC announced on August 10, 2026 a strategic partnership creating Theseus Infrastructure, a platform to develop, operate and lease data centers to Anthropic under long-term agreements.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic, Macquarie Asset Management, and GIC today announced a strategic partnership to establish Theseus Infrastructure, a new platform to develop, operate and lease data center infrastructure at scale to Anthropic under long-term agreements.

key_facts.fact: Funds managed by Macquarie Asset Management, together with GIC, will own the platform and fund the majority of the equity for each project, with Anthropic as anchor tenant and an initial focus on US sites.
key_facts.excerpt: The parties will work together to identify and develop new sites for which Anthropic will be the anchor tenant, with an initial focus on the United States. Funds managed by Macquarie Asset Management will, together with GIC, own the platform and fund the majority of the equity for each project.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic committed to cover electricity price increases that consumers might otherwise face from the new sites.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic will cover electricity price increases that consumers otherwise may face from these sites, in line with commitments it announced earlier this year.

key_facts.fact: The companies did not disclose spending plans or project sizes, saying only the facilities would be purpose-built and would 'require significant capital investment'.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies did not disclose spending plans or project sizes, saying only that the facilities would be "purpose-built to support Anthropic's growing capacity needs" and "require significant capital investment".

key_facts.fact: The structure shifts construction and ownership risk to infrastructure investors while Anthropic keeps capacity via leases; Anthropic had previously announced a $50 billion US data center program with Fluidstack in Texas and New York.
key_facts.excerpt: Today, we are announcing a $50 billion investment in American computing infrastructure, building data centers with Fluidstack in Texas and New York, with more sites to come.

stories.headline: Chinese makers shipped 97% of the world's humanoid robots in the first half of 2026

key_facts.fact: China's humanoid robot makers commanded more than 97% of global shipments in the first half of 2026, according to Smart Analytics Global data reported August 10.
key_facts.excerpt: China's humanoid robot makers commanded more than 97% of global shipments in the first half of 2026, according to new industry data affirming the country's early lead against US rivals in the burgeoning field.

key_facts.fact: Global humanoid shipments totaled roughly 19,100 units in H1 2026, more than triple the 5,100 units in the same period of 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Global humanoid robot shipments totaled roughly 19,100 units in the first half of 2026, more than triple the 5,100 units shipped in the same period last year, according to data from Smart Analytics Global.

key_facts.fact: The California-based research firm expects shipments to reach around 60,000 units this year and half a million by 2030.
key_facts.excerpt: The California-based research firm expects shipments to rise to around 60,000 units this year and reach half a million by 2030.

key_facts.fact: AgiBot shipped 5,168 units in 2025 for roughly 39% of the global market and Unitree moved over 5,000 units, so the two Chinese firms together accounted for more than half of all humanoids shipped worldwide.
key_facts.excerpt: AgiBot shipped 5,168 units in 2025, capturing roughly 39% of global market share on its own. Unitree moved over 5,000 units in the same period. Together, these two firms accounted for more than half of all humanoid robots shipped anywhere on the planet.

key_facts.fact: Most of the H1 2026 units were manufactured in Shenzhen and Hangzhou.
key_facts.excerpt: During the first six months of 2026, the 19,100 units shipped globally were overwhelmingly manufactured in Shenzhen and Hangzhou, eclipsing the 5,100 units recorded during the same period in 2025.

stories.headline: Moore Threads plans Hong Kong listing after first-half revenue jumps 147%

key_facts.fact: Chinese AI chip designer Moore Threads said in a filing released Sunday, August 9, that its board approved a plan to issue H shares and list on the main board of the Hong Kong stock exchange.
key_facts.excerpt: The Shanghai-listed company said on Sunday that its board had approved a plan to issue H shares and list on the main board of the Hong Kong stock exchange, a move designed to deepen the firm's "international strategic footprint", attract and retain talent, and "further enhance corporate governance and core competitiveness".

key_facts.fact: Revenue rose 147% year on year to 1.74 billion yuan ($252-258 million) in January-June, and the net loss narrowed to 11.6 million yuan ($1.72 million) from 270.9 million yuan a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: Moore Threads also reported a first-half net loss of 11.6 million yuan ($1.72 million), down from 270.9 million yuan in the same period last year, according to a separate filing. Revenue jumped 147% to 1.74 billion yuan in January-June.

key_facts.fact: The company's shares have surged more than 420% since its Shanghai STAR Market debut on December 5, 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: Artificial intelligence chipmaker Moore Threads Technology Co. said it plans to list in Hong Kong at an "appropriate time" after its shares have surged more than 420% since their Shanghai debut last year.

key_facts.fact: First-half gross profit reached 989 million yuan (up 103.78%) and R&D spending was 769 million yuan (up 38.16%), with flagship MTT S5000 GPUs deployed in Beijing, Wuxi and Hangzhou and its MUSA software stack supporting more than 800,000 developers.
key_facts.excerpt: Gross profit reached 989 million yuan, up 103.78 percent, while net losses attributable to shareholders narrowed sharply by 95.73 percent... Moore Threads maintained heavy research and development (R&D) spending of 769 million yuan in the first half, up 38.16 percent year-on-year... Its MUSA software stack now supports more than 800,000 developers.

key_facts.fact: Rival Chinese AI chipmaker Cambricon reported first-half revenue of 5.996 billion yuan, up 108.13%, with net profit up 122.61% to 2.311 billion yuan.
key_facts.excerpt: Fellow AI chip leader Cambricon also delivered equally robust results on Friday. Its first-half revenue hit 5.996 billion yuan, up 108.13 percent year-on-year, while net profit attributable to shareholders rose 122.61 percent to 2.311 billion yuan.

stories.headline: Memory crunch hits Apple: iPhone 18 Pro BOM up 38% as US rules block Chinese DRAM

key_facts.fact: TrendForce estimated on August 10 that the bill-of-materials cost of the 256GB iPhone 18 Pro will be about 38% higher year on year, led by memory prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Driven by soaring memory prices, TrendForce estimates that the BOM cost of the 256 GB iPhone 18 Pro, scheduled for release in the third quarter of 2026, will be approximately 38% higher than that of its 2025 predecessor.

key_facts.fact: Memory's share of the iPhone Pro's total BOM cost has risen from around 10% a year ago to roughly 34% in Q3 2026, and is expected to exceed 40% in the first half of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: An analysis of the 256 GB iPhone Pro models over the past two generations shows that memory's share of total BOM cost has risen dramatically—from around 10% a year ago to approximately 34% in 3Q26, and is expected to exceed 40% in 1H27.

key_facts.fact: Apple is testing DRAM from China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) for iPhones, MacBooks and other devices and is seeking White House approval to use the chips in China-market products.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple $AAPL has been evaluating memory chips from CXMT, a Chinese manufacturer, for use in products spanning its lineup — among them iPhones and MacBooks — according to Reuters. The company has held early talks with CXMT about supplying components, with an initial focus on devices sold in China. Apple is also seeking White House approval to use the chips in China-market products, according to Semafor.

key_facts.fact: US technology-transfer rules bar Apple from giving CXMT the technical specifications needed for custom memory, so any deal would be limited to standard parts; CXMT was added to restriction lists when 188 companies were included in June 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: under U.S. federal rules, U.S. companies cannot transfer technology to CXMT, including the technical details and product specification information for special chips Apple would use. That makes it effectively impossible for Apple to place orders with CXMT for made-to-order memory... CXMT was excluded at the time, but it was included in the restrictions when 188 companies were added in June 2026.

key_facts.fact: A bipartisan group of US senators wrote to Apple in July urging it not to buy Chinese chips, and analysts say CXMT's technology trails SK Hynix, Samsung and Micron by roughly two to three generations.
key_facts.excerpt: A bipartisan group of U.S. senators wrote to Apple in July urging the company not to pursue Chinese chips, according to Semafor... According to an analyst cited by CNBC, CXMT's technology lags the industry's front-runners — SK Hynix, Samsung, and Micron $MU — by roughly two to three generations.

key_facts.fact: The shortage traces to hyperscalers Google, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon expanding capex, which pushed memory and storage chip costs up fourfold as manufacturers diverted output to high-bandwidth memory for AI servers.
key_facts.excerpt: The shortage stems from hyperscalers including Google $GOOGL, Microsoft $MSFT, Meta $META, and Amazon $AMZN dramatically expanding capital expenditure budgets, which caused memory and storage chip costs to rise fourfold.

key_facts.fact: HP and Acer are already sourcing CXMT chips for products sold outside the United States.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple is not alone in turning to CXMT. HP $HPQ and Acer are already sourcing CXMT chips for products destined for markets beyond the United States, a step both companies have taken to help offset tightening supply, according to Reuters.
